Running graph_constraint(..., diagnose = TRUE) surfaces checks ran creating graph constraint object: individual values less equal 1 individual values greater equal 0 single NA value optimised, least 2 needed vector incomplete, sum elements must less 1. complete, sum must 1. values diagonal must 0. transition matrix square. values less equal 1. values greater equal 0. incomplete rows least 2 NA values complete rows sum equal 1. incomplete rows sum less 1. hypothesis weight constraint vector m elements, transition matrix m * m (vice versa). core pillar graph constraint validation comparison 1. Floating point arithmetic programming languages approximation real arithmetic. reason aim absolute comparison, rather want know , example, sum hypothesis weights close 1. close? Let’s look example. rely default graph_constraint() tolerance object built even thought sum complete hypothesis weight vector strictly equal 1: can control stringent comparison . example, setting tolerance 0 result check longer ignoring 10e-13 difference.

title: Optimise Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: multigrain (Multiple Testing using Graphical Approaches; Improve power Numerical Optimisation) R package finds optimal graphical multiple testing procedure clinical trial. Confirmatory trials routinely test multiple hypotheses — across endpoints, doses, subpopulations — must strongly control family-wise error rate (FWER). Graphical approaches popular framework , choosing hypothesis weights transition matrix make graph typically done hand. multigrain automates : given simulated p-values user-defined trial success measure (function scores possible pattern hypothesis rejections), searches hypothesis weights transition weights find graph maximises expected trial success. result valid graphical test strongly controls FWER. fixed-sample gain-function optimisation workflow implemented trial_success() graph_optimise() described Spiers et al. (2026), Gain-function optimisation graphical multiple testing procedures confirmatory clinical trials (arXiv:2609.19994v1).
